title: Reflow
body:
Reflow (also called layout) is the browser recalculating the geometry of elements — position, size, how everything else shifts as a result. It's the expensive half of the rendering pipeline, because changing one element's dimensions can force the browser to re-measure its ancestors, siblings, and descendants.

Anything that changes layout triggers it: adding or removing nodes, changing `width`, `height`, `font-size`, `display`, or reading a layout property like `offsetHeight` immediately after a write (which forces a synchronous reflow). The practical rule is to batch [[DOM]] mutations rather than interleaving reads and writes, and to animate with `transform` and `opacity`, which only trigger [[Repaint]] or compositing. See [[DOM Performance]].
